facts.fact: The Tanzania Bureau of Standards (TBS) published its list of new and revised compulsory Tanzania Standards as of October 2025, enforceable under the Standards Act, Cap. 130 (R.E. 2023), which shows a national standards body exists in law; the captured entries are on batteries, conductors, fasteners, wire and similar goods and name no standard on information technology, security, software or data, and the document says its list continues beyond the capture (published 2025-10, used as the date).

note: No certification fact: the document is a list of compulsory standards and names no certifier; no IT or data standard appears in the captured entries (excerpt only).

facts.fact: TCRA's Director General said the Tanzania Bureau of Standards (TBS) has newly introduced a Tanzania Standard on accessibility of communications and ICT products and services for persons with disabilities; the document gives no standard number or issue date (published 2026-10-09, used as the date).

note: No certification fact: TBS 'recognised' TCRA's website for implementing the accessibility standard, which is recognition, not certification, and no certifier or certificate is named.

facts.fact: The ISO member page says the Tanzania Bureau of Standards was established by the Standards Act of 1975, operational from 6 April 1976, with responsibility for formulating standards.

The Tanzania Bureau of Standards, under the Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade, is developing Tanzania standards and circulated drafts for comment, including ISO/IEC 23894, 27032, 27035, 27036 and 27043 adoptions.
